title: Prevent tenant operator starvation during on-prem upgrades; surgical state rehydrate & livepatch
creator: Jared Kim
description:
Summary: Several customers experienced tenant-level outages during private (on-prem/VPC) operator + Helm upgrades where a post-upgrade KV backfill combined with secret rotation caused the operator control loop to fall behind and eventually stop processing tenant CRs. This ticket coordinates a short-lived livepatch and a longer-term operator behaviour change to prevent operator starvation during heavy reconciliation windows.

Problem details: During recent staged rollouts we observed a pattern: when a Helm-driven upgrade triggers a schema hint migration and ExternalSecret refresh, it causes a large burst of tenant config mutations. The operator attempts to reconcile everything immediately, triggering expensive KV cache projections and leader-election churn. Under constrained kubelet CPU/cgroup limits on some customer nodes, this manifests as queue growth -> reconcile loop latency explosion -> leader re-election storms -> controller stalls where tenants become effectively unserved. The failure mode differs from a crash: the operator liveness probe stays green while reconcile throughput drops to near zero.

Goals: 1) Ship an emergency livepatch that adds a per-tenant reconciliation backoff + global admission gate to limit concurrent heavy reconciles during upgrade/fill jobs. 2) Provide an automated runbook and tenant-visibility dashboard for customers and SEs to detect and mitigate in-flight storms. 3) Implement a medium-term change: incremental KV backfill with rate-limiting and checkpointed rehydrate so upgrades can't saturate operator event loops.

Scope: Affects Private/VPC/on-prem operator behavior only. Hosted customers use different rollout paths and are not affected. Work split between runtime infra (controller changes and kvcache), operator packaging (Helm hooks), and SRE (runbook + monitoring).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Jared Kim: Triage call summary. Customer A (financial) reported full tenant degradation after operator helm upgrade. Reproduced in internal lab by simulating ExternalSecret rotation + CRD migration; operator displayed stalled reconcile throughput. Severity set to P0 and SE escalation opened.

2026-03-10 - Priya Desai: Initial mitigation: advised customers to scale operator replicas to 3 and temporarily pause Helm post-upgrade hooks that trigger mass mutations. This reduced immediate customer impact but is not an acceptable long-term fix.

2026-03-11 - Enginfra: Reproduced locally with a 10k-tenant synthetic; root cause narrowed to uncontrolled concurrent rehydrates that trigger expensive kvcache checkpoint writes. Adding crude mutex around heavy reconcile loop allowed throughput to recover in lab.

2026-03-11 - Priya Desai: Drafted livepatch plan: 1) admission gate flag ENABLE_RECONCILE_TAPER (off by default for new installs, on for quick emergency rollout), 2) per-tenant exponential backoff after N heavy ops, 3) rate-limiter for background kvcache rehydrate. Will ship as operator-2026.03.1 hotpatch.

2026-03-11 - QA: Nightly integration created with 1k synthetic tenants to validate stability. Early runs show 70% reduction in peak reconcile concurrency and restored controller responsiveness under the same mutation workload.
2026-03-12 - Security: Reviewed livepatch changes; no new secrets stored and HSM/KMS calls unchanged. Marked security_review_required false. TODO: include audit logging for gated rehydrates.

2026-03-12 - Priya Desai: Created customer communication bullet points and emergency KB for SEs explaining temporary mitigations and required operator flags. Link to KB: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/ENG-821997+-+Tenant+Operator+Starvation+Runbook

2026-03-12 - Enginfra: Opened PR #1429 that implements admission gate + per-tenant backoff and a basic token-bucket rate limiter for kvcache rehydrates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1429. CI green on unit tests; integration tests ongoing.
2026-03-12 - Customer Success: Notified impacted customers of planned hotpatch deployment windows and rollback criteria. Requesting approval to schedule canary for two low-risk tenants tonight.

2026-03-12 - Priya Desai: Added follow-ups: 1) Postmortem draft due 2026-03-18, 2) Medium-term design doc for incremental rehydrate checkpointing (ENG-822500 placeholder), 3) Console dashboard tile for per-tenant reconcile-latency (console-2026.04).
acceptance_criteria: Livepatch deployed to canary tenants without increasing error budget or causing new reconciler crashes
Per-tenant reconcile concurrency never exceeds configurable threshold under synthetic 10k mutation workload
SE runbook validated by CS with at least two customer escalations simulated and clear mitigation steps
Integration tests cover kvcache rate limiter and checkpoint roll-forward/rollback
next_steps: Merge PR #1429 and cut operator-2026.03.1 hotpatch branch
Deploy hotpatch to 2 canary tenants tonight (22:00 UTC) and monitor reconcile-latency + leader-election churn
If canary stable for 4h, schedule broad rollout during next maintenance window and publish KB to customers
Begin design work for ENG-822500: incremental checkpointed kvcache rehydrate with resume tokens
